claims.statement: PSE's current redispatch rules distinguish renewable sources equipped with active-power control and describe reduction objects by location, technology, power, and control mode; the founder can obtain a founder-accessible control route by installing a cross-brand gateway on commercial PV sites, contracting dispatch and measurement rights, and controlling eligible flexible on-site loads such as EV charging, hot water, refrigeration, or storage through the family installer channel.

PSE states that non-market redispatch reduces renewable generation when surplus remains after market balancing and reports 26020 MW of Polish PV installed by 1 February 2026; it has issued multi-day PV reduction orders with a right to compensation for energy that would otherwise have been produced, making curtailed kilowatt-hours, claim leakage, and unused on-site flexibility observable losses.

Commercial PV owners and portfolio managers bear production and claim-reconciliation losses during ordered reductions and already spend on O&M, metering, batteries, energy management, and compensation preparation; the payer is the site or portfolio owner when a curtailment-prone installation can redirect energy lawfully behind the meter or improve evidence for a compensation claim.

contrary_evidence: PSE provides a compensation route for eligible non-market redispatch, which can reduce the owner's incentive to buy avoidance technology and may make claim assistance more valuable than physical load shifting.

A reduction order may require lower generation rather than merely lower grid export; redirecting energy behind the meter might not be permitted or credited, and this must be resolved before any dispatch pilot.

economics.acquisition_route: Use the family installer to screen 30 commercial PV owners for ordered reductions, interval meters, and flexible loads; pre-sell five measurement-only gateways and run shadow dispatch plus compensation reconciliation before enabling automatic control.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A cross-brand fleet of 20000 commercial sites at an assumed 300-600 PLN monthly platform fee plus hardware margin and a bounded share of verified recovered value could become a Polish flexibility and performance-data asset, with later revenue from aggregators or energy-service partners if regulation permits.
economics.founder_time: Approximately 12-18 founder hours per week for dispatch modeling, device integrations, and channel management; installation, electrical work, and site service are delegated.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Preliminary 65-80% contribution margin on subscription and savings share after gateway support and data costs, with 15-30% hardware margin; field-service frequency could reduce this materially.
economics.payback: Offer automatic control only when a shadow season shows that lawful self-consumption, better claim evidence, or avoided peak-energy purchases can repay hardware and fees within 24 months; high-value sites may qualify while most do not.
economics.pricing: Assumed 3000-8000 PLN installed gateway, 250-700 PLN per site per month, and 10-20% of independently measured recovered energy value or additional compensation.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Forecasting, monitoring, dispatch readiness, and claim evidence recur every month and on every redispatch interval; the contracted device fleet remains useful across changing tariffs and flexibility markets.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Site-level curtailment exposure, counterfactual production, flexible-load response, inverter behavior, claim acceptance, and local grid-event patterns across brands.
fingerprint.customer: Polish commercial and small utility-scale PV owners with controllable on-site loads, batteries, or recurring redispatch exposure.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable installers, O&M firms, energy auditors, battery integrators, and claim advisers screen their installed base and bundle the gateway during service or retrofit visits.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A cross-brand gateway and contracted control fleet that first measures curtailment exposure, then lawfully schedules on-site flexible demand and produces counterfactual claim evidence; revenue is hardware, subscription, and recovered-value share.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A PV owner pays from O&M, energy-management, storage, or recovered-generation budget when PSE orders reduction or forecasts reveal repeated surplus periods.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A PV site receives or is exposed to non-market redispatch while flexible consumption, storage, and compensation evidence remain uncoordinated across separate vendor systems.

founder_fit: The parents' renewable company offers unusually direct distribution, installation capacity, and real operating sites.
Counterfactual generation, event forecasting, and device optimization use the founder's data-science skills.
A measurement-only five-site pilot is part-time, reversible, and below available capital before any automated dispatch or market commitment.
risks: Dispatching electrical loads or generation without clear grid and safety authorization could create serious regulatory and equipment liability.
Cross-brand device integration and field support may turn into low-margin custom installation work.
Inverter OEMs, retailers, battery vendors, and licensed aggregators can bundle the same controls and use existing customer fleets.

structure.control_point: Installed cross-brand gateways plus contractual dispatch, measurement, and counterfactual-data rights at PV sites.
structure.critical_dependency: Grid rules must permit valuable behind-the-meter response during curtailment, or compensation-evidence uplift alone must justify the gateway.

thesis: Polish PV curtailment has become an observable operating event rather than a theoretical grid risk. A founder-accessible installer channel can place cross-brand gateways at affected commercial sites, control the measurement and dispatch contract, and coordinate flexible on-site demand with claim evidence; the fleet's response data can compound into a flexibility asset even if hardware vendors commoditize individual controllers.
title: PV Curtailment-Recovery Control Fleet
uncertainties: Does Polish redispatch treatment permit or reward behind-the-meter load shifting during an ordered reduction?
How many family-channel and adjacent commercial sites have enough curtailment exposure and flexible load for sub-two-year payback?
Can counterfactual production and compensation uplift be measured independently enough to support a savings share?
